identity.trade: Honey and beeswax: Amberley's hives line every hedge, and its candles light the shrines of the whole outer road.

greeting: Sit, if you like. No sermon unless you ask. I am out of sermons anyway.
All are welcome. Some are more welcome, depending on their boots.
rumour: Fewer come to the vigil. More come to the stones. I count both.
The envoy's men were seen at the crossroads. They bless nothing and write everything.
The hive in the old tower hums in a key nobody can name.

opinions.emmet_fellows: I would trust Emmet with a purse. A small one.

time.morning: Morning prayers are done. You are welcome in the garden.

dialogue.aside: Come in, sit, eat. I will hear no argument.

greeting: Rooms are clean. The beds are honest about their age.
Peace on your road. Mind the step, it is older than the faith.
rumour: Pilgrims eat modestly and drink modestly. The rooms are clean and the profit is modest.
Travellers say the stones are dimmer on the east road. I water the ale, not the news.
A pilgrim fell asleep at the shrine and woke speaking a tongue nobody knows. He is perfectly well.
The Amberley Apiary was busy last week. Something is stirring, or somebody is.

opinions.otto_strand: Otto undercuts me. I forgive Otto. Mostly.

time.evening: Evening vigil begins at dusk. Quiet, please.

dialogue.aside: Eh? Oh, it is you. I heard that. I always hear friends.

greeting: Bring iron or bring coin. Preferably iron.
The Amberley Apiary is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: Candle snuffers, lamp hooks, reliquary hinges. The faith has small needs and fussy ones.
Good steel is dear. Bad steel is dearer, the day it breaks.
A candle burned all night at the shrine, though none lit it.

opinions.godric_woolcott: Godric has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Godric.
opinions.gwen_thorpe: Gwen undercuts me. I forgive Gwen. Mostly.

time.night: Late. The shrine lamp is lit. You may sit.

dialogue.aside: Ah. You. Let me look at you a moment. Fine. You pass. Come in.

greeting: Everything has a price. Some of it is even written down.
Strangers in Amberley get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: Candles, incense and a rack of small bells. Pilgrims buy the bells and lose them.
Sold three lanterns today. People are afraid of the dark again.
The bell rings itself at odd hours. We stopped checking.
Whatever you hear about Amberley, half of it is true. We argue about which half.

opinions.flora_thorpe: Flora and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.
opinions.otto_strand: Otto undercuts me. I forgive Otto. Mostly.

time.rain: Rain on the shrine roof. A fine sound and a leaking corner.

dialogue.aside: Welcome. Wipe your boots. Please. Soap is dear and floors are dearer.

greeting: If it hurts it is working. If it does not hurt, you overpaid.
First time in Amberley? The Amberley Apiary is the place to start.
rumour: Willowbark is short. Everyone has a headache this season. Draw your own conclusions.
Pilgrims come in greater numbers and ask harder questions.
Amberley mead is stronger than it tastes. Travellers learn once.

opinions.flora_thorpe: Flora is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.morning: Morning prayers are done. You are welcome in the garden.

dialogue.aside: Welcome. Wipe your boots. Please. Soap is dear and floors are dearer.

greeting: Sit by me. My knees insist.
You will hear Amberley before you see it. Ask at the Amberley Apiary.
rumour: I remember the Long Dark. Nobody asks. Nobody wants the answer.
The almonry has more mouths than bread and more bread than it should. We pray over the arithmetic.

opinions.wolfram_marlowe: Wolfram lives next door and hears everything I do.

time.evening: Evening vigil begins at dusk. Quiet, please.

dialogue.aside: Punctual as ever. I would say a pun-ctual friend, but you heard it last time.

greeting: Smell that? That is patience, melted.
Welcome to Amberley. Mind the Amberley Apiary. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: Candles burn quicker lately. Same wax, same wick. The flame is hungrier.
The offering bowl is heavier each morning. We have not counted. We are afraid to.
A swarm settled on the shrine road and will not leave.

opinions.poppy_chandler: Poppy lives next door and hears everything I do.
opinions.una_swale: Una knows the trade. I will say that for Una.

time.night: Late. The shrine lamp is lit. You may sit.

dialogue.aside: Good to see you. Now, what do you need, and what can you spare?

greeting: Never swat. Bow. They notice manners.
Folk come to Amberley for honey and beeswax. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: Candles burn longer if you hum while you pour. Nobody knows why.
A traveller left a gift at the shrine and no name. A gold ring. Real gold.
If trade slows, Amberley feels it first. If it speeds up, Amberley feels it last.

opinions.halla_lauds: Halla is good company and better at keeping quiet.
opinions.ingram_hornby: Ingram knows the trade. I will say that for Ingram.

time.rain: Rain on the shrine roof. A fine sound and a leaking corner.

dialogue.aside: There you are. I was just thinking of you, which is rare, and a compliment.

greeting: The road east is shut. The road west is long. Choose.
Sit, if you like. Silence is free.
rumour: A rider crossed at night with a sunlit banner under his cloak.
The old tales say the stones were once voices. Now they hum. Is that better or worse?

opinions.derwin_kemble: Derwin and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.
opinions.hamo_fothergill: Hamo works hard and talks harder.

time.morning: Morning prayers are done. You are welcome in the garden.

dialogue.aside: You look tired, friend. I will not lie. Rest.

greeting: Day work, day pay. What is it?
Amberley is honey and beeswax. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Dug a drain and hit a flat stone with marks on it. The foreman said fill it in. I did.
Someone has been mending the shrine wall at night. Mortar, still wet, in the morning.
Ask anyone in Amberley about the Amberley Apiary. You will get four stories and one fact.

opinions.hedda_greaves: Hedda lives next door and hears everything I do.
opinions.wolfram_marlowe: Wolfram knows the trade. I will say that for Wolfram.

time.evening: Evening vigil begins at dusk. Quiet, please.

dialogue.aside: Tell me everything. No, truly. I will not ask twice. I will ask three times.

greeting: The stones are not our rivals. Ask the envoys.
Amberley is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: Pilgrims bring stories and I do not know which to believe. I believe the ones with muddy boots.
When Amberley is quiet we say it is peaceful. When it is very quiet we say nothing.

opinions.una_swale: Una keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.night: Late. The shrine lamp is lit. You may sit.

dialogue.aside: I dreamed of you last night. You were a heron. It suited you.

greeting: Walk slowly. They notice hurry. They respect calm.
rumour: Wild bees nest in the old tower. Nobody wants that honey.
The Amberley Apiary has seen odder days than this. Nobody remembers when.

opinions.emmet_fellows: Emmet works hard and talks harder.
opinions.hamo_fothergill: Hamo knows the trade. I will say that for Hamo.

time.rain: Rain on the shrine roof. A fine sound and a leaking corner.

dialogue.aside: Take something. Anything. No, a bigger something. I insist.

greeting: Soil does not care who you are. It cares what you do on Tuesdays.
rumour: The field by the hedge goes quiet at dusk. No crickets. I stopped sowing there.
Every few years Amberley has a winter nobody forgets. The old folk say this one is early.

opinions.ingram_hornby: Ingram knows the trade. I will say that for Ingram.
opinions.wendel_kemble: Wendel works hard and talks harder.

time.morning: Morning prayers are done. You are welcome in the garden.

dialogue.aside: A bright day and a bright friend! What luck!

greeting: Do you have a dog? I do not have a dog. Yet.
rumour: The big kids say there is a ghost in the barn. I have not checked. Yet.
The envoy's men were seen at the crossroads. They bless nothing and write everything.

opinions.wendel_kemble: Wendel is blood. That settles most arguments and starts the rest.

greeting: I am not lost. I am exploring.
rumour: Our dog knows something and will not say what.
The bell rings itself at odd hours. We stopped checking.

opinions.blythe_merrow: I would trust Blythe with a purse. A small one.
opinions.gwen_thorpe: Gwen is blood. That settles most arguments and starts the rest.

clues.note: A candle stub on the sill, burned to the stump and doused with a thumb.
The offering count has two hands in it. One is the almoner's. The other is trying to be.
A scrap of a pilgrim's cloak, caught on a nail far from the pilgrim road.

stashes.say: You carry four split logs from the woodpile.
You wrap two jars of lamp oil in straw.
